entries.entry_title: Browser SDK v3 guides are retired
entries.entry_body: The Browser SDK v3 guides are removed and v3 is now reference-only, matching v2. The v3 and Click-to-Call reference documentation is unchanged, and the old guide URLs redirect. Note that v4 does not yet implement recording, RTMP streaming, or interactive live streaming, which some removed guides covered.
entries.reasoning: A removal of published pages, which the rubric lists under notable. Also a URL change, but removal is the higher tier.
entries.internal_detail: Ten published v3 guides were deleted and four redirects added covering both /v3/js/guides* and legacy /js/guides* paths. Anyone who bookmarked or was sent a v3 guide link now lands on a redirect target rather than the guide. If a customer needs recording, RTMP streaming, or interactive live streaming, v4 does not implement those yet — that gap is real, not a documentation omission.

entries.reasoning: Adds an analytics tracking script via a js: block in docs.yml. Tooling; nothing a reader can do or know differently.
Converts CRLF to LF across 67 SWML pages and drops legacy id: frontmatter. Formatting and internal metadata only, with no reader-visible change.
Capitalization fix, RELAY to Relay, across 125 files. Explicitly listed under skip, and flagged mechanical.
Removes a cache-busting JSX comment from the homepage. No rendered change.
Adds the same cache-busting comment #541 removed. No rendered change.

entries.entry_title: E911 registration is self-service through the REST API
entries.entry_body: You can now register an emergency address and enable E911 on a number yourself, instead of filing a support ticket. The E911 guide covers creating a carrier-validated address, assigning it to a number, and waiting for `e911_status` to become `active`, with examples rendered from the API spec.
entries.reasoning: Documents a newly available self-service capability replacing a manual process. Carries a factual correction about porting as well, but notable is the higher tier.
entries.internal_detail: The E911 guide no longer tells customers to open a ticket — the native REST endpoints are live and the flow is self-service. Two related corrections ship with it: the phone numbers page now points at the REST API for programmatic management, and the porting guide now states that E911 registrations do not transfer with a port, replacing the old advice to contact SignalWire before submitting the order. Expect fewer E911 provisioning tickets, and redirect any that arrive to the guide.

entries.entry_body: Groq, Mistral, Grok, Smallest.ai, Fish Audio, and Speechify are documented as text-to-speech engines, each with its models, voices, and usage. The `groq-tts` engine replaces the retired `playai-turbo`. Rime's `arcana` model is deprecated in favor of `coda`.
entries.reasoning: Six new pages plus new accepted engine values in the SWML reference. Squarely notable.
entries.internal_detail: Six new engine reference pages, plus the previously missing amazon, azure, and openai entries in the SWML ai.languages engine list. Two things to watch: anyone still on playai-turbo must move to groq-tts, and Rime arcana is end-of-life in favor of coda. The Groq Arabic model additionally requires accepting Canopy Labs' terms in the Groq console or requests fail. Voice widgets for groq-tts, mistral, smallest, fish, and speechify may render empty until the CDN voice catalog picks up those engines.

entries.entry_title: Only catalog voices resolve, and custom voice options are documented
entries.entry_body: The Cartesia and ElevenLabs pages state that only voices from SignalWire's catalog resolve, and the voices page documents what is available for custom and cloned voices.
entries.reasoning: Borderline. It is a clarification that changes what a reader concludes, which the rubric puts at minor. No new page actually shipped despite the PR description, so the notable criterion for a new page is not met.
entries.internal_detail: Readers were assuming any valid provider voice ID would work, because catalog IDs are opaque UUIDs. It does not — it fails at call time with an audible fallback, which is the symptom to listen for on a ticket. Warnings now say so on both provider pages, and a Custom and cloned voices section on the voices page states the real options: ElevenLabs voice import is available by request through Support, and Cartesia custom voices are not supported. Note the PR description calls this a new page at /voice/tts/custom-voices, but it shipped as an anchored section on the voices page instead.

entries.reasoning: Adds llms.txt discovery hints for AI agents: a navbar link and a visually hidden snippet. No new capability or documented behavior, and Support will not field questions about it. Low confidence because the navbar link is a visible site change, so a reviewer may want this reported.

entries.entry_title: Status callbacks are documented as advisory, not realtime triggers
entries.entry_body: Status callbacks are best-effort notifications: one can arrive late or never arrive at all, and a missed callback is invisible to your server. Do not gate time-critical or business-critical actions solely on receiving one. The webhooks page describes the alternatives, including Relay over WebSocket, REST confirmation and reconciliation, and in-call flow logic.
entries.reasoning: Sits between minor and notable. Chose notable because it adds substantial new guidance and a canonical linkable section about reliability that developers may have built around, rather than only correcting a sentence.
entries.internal_detail: The platform webhooks page previously implied callbacks were a reliable realtime signal, saying applications could react to each state change as it happens. That line is gone, replaced by a canonical Status callbacks are advisory section, linkable at #status-callback-reliability. A shared advisory note is now embedded on every page documenting status callbacks, and the same wording is in the TypeSpec descriptions so it reaches the REST reference. Use the anchor when a customer reports missed callbacks: the answer is to confirm state via GET or move to Relay, not to expect delivery guarantees. One retry detail also changed on the common webhook errors page.

entries.entry_title: Relay client examples no longer set an invalid host
entries.entry_body: The Relay client guide drops the `host` parameter from its examples.
entries.reasoning: A corrected factual error in a code example that previously showed an invalid value. The rubric puts corrections and non-running examples at minor.
entries.internal_detail: The old examples passed host="your-space.signalwire.com", which is not a valid Relay host — anyone who copied them was configuring something wrong. External users never need host at all; it defaults to relay.signalwire.com, correct for all public-cloud customers. The parameter is still documented in the SDK relay/client reference along with the default and the SIGNALWIRE_SPACE environment variable.

entries.entry_title: New guide for AI tool calling
entries.entry_body: A new tool calling guide covers the mental model where the AI agent runs the conversation and your code owns the business logic, how a SWAIG function works, and a complete order-status agent in both SWML and the Python Server SDK. The best practices guide is rewritten around writing for realtime voice, speech-recognition hints, and testing with post-prompt reports.
entries.reasoning: A new guide plus a major rewrite of an existing one. New page is a notable criterion.
entries.internal_detail: New page at /docs/platform/ai/tool-calling, and a substantially rewritten best practices guide. The AI overview and capabilities pages gained a how-it-works section and an AI in the media path section. Two naming and path changes matter for old links: the Agents SDK to Server SDKs rename is now complete across platform, server-sdks, and SWML pages, and stale /docs/swml/reference/ai paths were fixed. The Amazon Bedrock SWAIG includes reference page was removed.
